classification.difficultyReason: Derive equations from a folding construction, solve their intersection and interpret its position as a third of the paper's width.

inlines.text: A square sheet of paper can be folded into perfect thirds using the sequence of folds shown below.
Explain how this works by finding the point of intersection of the two lines shown below.

inlines.text: . The intersection is one third of the paper's width from the right edge; symmetry gives the other thirds crease.

answer.worked:
The corner-to-corner line has equation $y=x$. The other line passes through $(0,1)$ and $(1,-1)$.
$$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{-1-1}{1-0}\\m&=-2\\y&=-2x+1\end{align*}$$
At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}x&=-2x+1\\3x&=1\\x&=\frac13\\y&=\frac13\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $\left(\frac13,\frac13\right)$. The square has width $2$, and the horizontal distance from this point to the right edge is $1-\frac13=\frac23$, which is one third of that width. The symmetric intersection gives a crease one third of the width from the left edge, so the two vertical creases divide the paper into three equal strips.
